notes: Four items queued from the 2026-09-17 poll, all read. Every one of these articles carries a related-articles rail repeating the other three; those hits all land above 90 per cent into the page and are furniture, not reporting.

coverage.note: 77 Beale Street appears in the Fifty at First piece only as a height comparison against another project in the pipeline, and the list of reawakened projects in the 395 3rd Street piece (321 Florida, 360 Fifth, 400 Divisadero, 2918 Mission, 469 Stevenson) is quoted from a Chronicle report; neither says anything about those buildings.

findings.description: The San Francisco Recovery Fund announced its vision for the mothballed 50 1st Street site, formerly the Oceanwide Center, renamed Fifty at First: a 915-foot commercial office tower of about 1.5 million square feet across 56 floors, with roughly 20,000 square feet of outdoor space and an arts programme in consultation with SFMOMA, targeted to open as early as 2031. Construction on the site ceased in 2020. Permits had not been published when the article ran. The project is proposed and not built, so nothing goes in the building block.

citation.label: San Francisco YIMBY, “Oceanwide Center No More, Renderings Revealed For Fifty at First, San Francisco,” 17 September 2026

raw.text: The San Francisco Recovery Fund has announced its vision for 50 1st Street in SoMa, San Francisco. The site has been a prominent mothballed pit in the heart of the city after construction ceased in 2020

publish.note: Published on /san-francisco/east-cut/1st-street/42/, which already existed — EAS puts 42 and 50 1st Street on parcel 3708055, so per the directory contract the page is at the lower number even though the story prints 50. The page's own 2010 entry already describes this site as the one proposed for a three-tower development, so the entry lands in the right place. Fifty at First is proposed and unpermitted, so the whole project team stays in extra and nothing enters the building block. The card is on the homepage news grid.

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 50 01ST ST → parcel 3708055; sf-parcels has blklot 3708055 active, 42–50 01ST; the 2025 roll records it as miscellaneous/mixed-use, built 1917. EAS puts 42, 50 01ST ST on that parcel, so per the directory contract the fact belongs on one page at the lowest, 42. The record writes the street 1ST; EAS holds the numbered streets zero-padded to four characters, so this is 01ST.

findings.description: Preliminary permits were refiled for a residential tower at 395 3rd Street in SoMa, now proposed as a 45-storey, 480-foot building with 501 apartments of which 51 would be deed-restricted affordable. Earlier applications were for 35 storeys and 522 apartments, then 37 storeys and 53 affordable units. The application invokes Senate Bill 423 and the State Density Bonus law. The project is proposed and not built, so nothing goes in the building block.

citation.label: San Francisco YIMBY, “Plans Refiled for 395 3rd Street in SoMa, San Francisco,” 15 September 2026

raw.text: Preliminary permits have been refiled for a residential tower at 395 3rd Street in SoMa, San Francisco. The project team is seeking re-entitlement for the site and now proposes a 45-story skyscraper with 501 apartments

publish.note: Published on /san-francisco/east-cut/3rd-street/395/, which already existed. Proposed and not built, so the architects and sponsor stay in extra. The card is on the homepage news grid.

findings.description: Renderings were published for the larger of the two buildings in the residential infill at 70 and 74 Laidley Street in Fairmount Heights: a roughly 40-foot, four-storey apartment building of about 6,040 square feet, with four studios, a one-bedroom and a two-bedroom penthouse, a shared living space on the second floor and a four-car ground-level garage connecting to a studio at 74 Laidley Street. Construction is estimated at about $8 million. The article says the property owner is a San Francisco-based individual, which the site does not record. The project is proposed and not built, so nothing goes in the building block.

extra.cladding: limestone tiles, smooth concrete, stucco, teak wood panels

citation.label: San Francisco YIMBY, “Renderings Revealed For 70-74 Laidley Street, San Francisco,” 16 September 2026

raw.text: Plans have been published for a portion of the residential infill at 70 and 74 Laidley Street in Fairmount Heights, San Francisco. Renderings have been published for the larger four-story apartment complex at 70 Laidley Street.

findings.note: The same project appears as backfill-2026-04-0013, recorded from the April 2026 article as 62 Laidley Street and pending because 62, 70 and 74 are three separate active parcels. That finding is about the proposal as a whole; this one is about the renderings for the 70 Laidley Street building specifically, and the article names 70 as the building it depicts.
